with_model_outputs.label: D1 after a rewarded visit to S2
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), and only when the reward input is 1 and the previous trial reached S2. Inside the window, (D1 & in_rew==1 & previous state == S2) has dev precision 1.00 with zero false positives. Almost all misses fall on the first trial of the window (rel -3), where the previous state lies outside the window. For those steps the predicate uses the agent upcoming choice a2 as a stand-in (it is computed by the agent, not a future random outcome). Combined dev score: P 0.99, R 0.97, F1 0.98. It does not fire on rewarded S1 visits (precision 0.001) or on unrewarded trials. Magnitude is nearly binary (median 2.39, about 0.8 of max). The top-quartile activations are somewhat enriched for surprising S2 rewards: S2 reached by a rare a1 transition, or S2 rewarded while S1 is the good state. This effect is modest (about 12-16% of the top quartiles vs about 3-4% of the bottom quartile). Recorded predicate uses only observed variables plus the agent own upcoming choice.

issues: Minor: the rel -3 fallback uses the agent's upcoming choice a2 as a stand-in for 'previous state was S2', which falls outside the window. Purely observed in-window, (D1 & in_rew==1 & prev_state==2) gets dev precision 1.00, recall 0.76, F1 0.87. The recall gap is all on rel -3 steps, so it comes from the window edge, not from the feature. At rel -3 the a2 proxy has precision 0.96; a1 has 0.026.

The feature tracks the previous state, not the upcoming action. Outside rel -3: rewarded, prev_state S2, upcoming a1 gives precision 1.00 (6357 steps); rewarded, prev_state S1, upcoming a2 gives precision 0.006. Rewarded S2 reached by a rare transition from a1 has precision 1.00. So the label's 'visit to S2' wording is correct; the choice that led there does not matter.

Never firing at GO or D2 is confirmed: 0 activations out of 380k steps each. Unrewarded D1 steps account for 2.2% of activations (2769 steps), but these are tiny, about 0.02-0.03 of max, so this is scattered noise. There are 0 activations at in_rew = -1.
Test-split misses and false positives are the rel -3 proxy errors plus very weak activations at in_rew==0. They hold 0.7% of the activation mass, and no systematic class showed up.
The magnitude-enrichment claim checks out: surprising S2 rewards (rare transition, or S1 is the good state) cover 3.2% / 7.4% / 17.3% / 13.6% of the activation quartiles, bottom to top.
Reported test scores reproduce: precision 0.990, recall 0.971, F1 0.980, mass recall 0.993.
